title: Dynamic credits for interactive UX (scratchpad)
content:
Notes to self - brainstorming a lightweight credits model for highly interactive UIs (chat widgets, inline suggestions).  Aim: simple to explain to product, friendly for short-turn micro-interactions, defensible unit economics so we don't lose money on high rps apps.

Assumptions (hosted avg cost -> internal):
- avg infra cost per 1M tokens (after batching/cache savings) = $8.5 (example; includes GPU amort + infra + overhead)
- avg tokens per micro-request = 80 (prompt+response combined)
- typical micro-session = 15–25 requests -> per-session tokens = 1.2k–2.0k
- target gross margin = 70% on hosted (so price should be ~3.3x cost)

Quick math:
- cost per token = $8.5 / 1,000,000 = $0.0000085/token
- cost per micro-request (80 tokens) = 80 * 0.0000085 = $0.00068/request
- desired price per request = 0.00068 * 3.3 ≈ $0.00224 (~0.22¢)

Credits framing (UX):
- make credits intuitive: 1 credit = baseline unit for a 100-token micro-turn.
- map: 1 credit ≈ 100 tokens ≈ $0.00085 cost -> price to customer ~ $0.0028 (rounded to $0.003)
- for larger completions use token multiplier (e.g., 1 credit per 100 tokens, fractional credits allowed but rounded on invoice).

Tier sketches:
- Free: 500 credits/mo (good for trial widgets; ~5k tokens)
- Starter: 10k credits/mo ($30/mo) — aimed at SMBs doing light embed/chat use
- Pro: 200k credits/mo ($420/mo) — heavy interactive usage, includes pref by region
- Enterprise: custom, volume discounts, committed reservations (mix of credits + reserved capacity)

Discount/scale rules (rough):
- 10–25% off credits at 500k+ monthly usage
- committed reservations (Dedicated) replace credits pricing; provide lower unit rates + SLAs

Edge cases and policy:
- caching: prefix reuse should be credited at a much lower rate (e.g., cache-hit = 10% of tokens billed) to encourage safe reuse
- replays/bot traffic: include rate-based throttles and anomaly credits deduction rules (manual review for suspect bursts)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should UI show credits as "tokens" or "actions"? (actions simpler for product)
- How to handle function calls / tool-invocations where token usage unpredictable? Proposal: bill by token at backend and surface as estimated credits to user; round down for UX simplicity but reconcile monthly.
- Investigate UX friction if fractional credits shown; maybe show "credits remaining" with nearest integer and an activity log.
- Build quick simulation: input: avg tokens per turn, turns per session, daily active users -> monthly credits burn. Hook to billing page for forecast.

Mini simulation example (to paste into spreadsheet):
- avg_tokens_per_turn = 80
- turns_per_session = 20
- sessions_per_user_per_day = 3
- MAU = 5,000
-> monthly_tokens = 80 * 20 * 3 * 5000 * 30 = 720,000,000 tokens (~720M)
-> credits (1 per 100 tokens) = 7.2M credits -> cost to us = 720M * 0.0000085 = $6,120 -> price at 3.3x = $20,196/month -> unit price per credit ~ $0.0028

Notes: these numbers are preliminary and intentionally conservative on cost. Need to iterate with infra finance to get more accurate per-model-per-length profiles (small models cheaper, long-sequence models more expensive). Also talk to growth about presentation (credits vs direct token pricing).

Random UX ideas: show "estimated sessions left" in console (converts credits -> sessions), and a "burst buffer" for interactive apps (small free burst credits that replenish slowly to absorb short spikes).

End of scratchpad. Revisit after infra provides per-model baseline costs (JIRA:PRIC-214) and after product decides on actions-as-unit vs tokens-as-unit.
